items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: Kay Starr came in and I thought oh Wheel of Fortune. No, she was a heck of a jazz singer.

ctx.x: When you got into doing this work in clubs singing and playing, I’ve done a bit of that, and you can tell when people are coming up to the piano to make a request and you know you sort of cross your fingers, you try to keep playing with your fingers crossed. Did you have occasion, because in the mid- to late-‘50s rock & roll was starting to make the airwaves and I wondered if you got requests in that genre that you had to like — oh I’m thinking of like Kay Starr “The Rock & Roll Waltz,” things that were changing…

Yes. Well what was her big hit, because I couldn’t believe it when I heard her. She came in, well I mean this is years later, to — was it Condon’s that had this afternoon or early evening thing, and Kay Starr came in and I thought oh Wheel of Fortune. No, she was a heck of a jazz singer. And of course there were a lot of those like Rosemary Clooney and Patti Page, who were really good singers but then they had to sing the stuff that was coming in now. And Mitch Miller — we all know about him.
Oh right. And “How Much is that Doggie in the Window” etcetera.
